description: Issue #125 / ADR §3.5 stage 2: `gates:` (declaring a NEW command) is now READ rather than refused. The definition travels in the execution contract's `verify.gateDefinitions` (CommandMate #1791), so nothing is ever written into the worktree's `.commandmate/verify.yaml` — which is what unblocked it: that file stays in the work-evidence change set on purpose (an agent weakening its own judge must stay detectable), while the contract is already snapshotted into `tasks.contract_json` and already excluded. The transcription is a COPY: author order, the author's `command` with its quotes removed, and `timeoutSec` ABSENT on the entry that declared none — so CommandMate's own default applies instead of a number this planner invented. `require:` and `gates:` coexist in one block and share one id space. The run is clean: reading a `gates:` block raises no warning at all.
